DEV-4231: Drive the keepalive test with fake timers

### Context
The PR fixes the flaky `unit` test that fails with `the keepalive never ticked` in `runner/pipeline/container-keepalive-slept.test.mjs`.

- **Why:** The test waited 500 event-loop turns for a real 5 ms keepalive timer. 500 turns take about 7 ms locally, so a faster loop ran out before the timer fired.
- **What changed:**
  - `runner/pipeline/container-keepalive-slept.test.mjs`: the keepalive `setInterval` runs on `t.mock.timers`, and each answer advances the clock by one interval. `setTimeout` and `setImmediate` stay real.
  - The same file now asserts that a slept session is not pinged again, which the first test's name already claimed.
- **Result:** The test no longer depends on machine speed or load. A keepalive that never fires still fails with the same message.

### Types of changes
- [ ] New example
- [ ] Update to an existing example
- [ ] README / documentation change
- [x] Demo runner (`runner/`) change
- [ ] CI / tooling change

### How was this verified?
- Old helper with a 20 ms interval: fails every run with `the keepalive never ticked`. The new helper passes at 5 ms and at 60 000 ms.
- 50 runs of the file at concurrency 8 with 11 CPU burners: 100/100 tests pass.
- Temporary changes to the built runtime, each reverted, all caught:
  - no keepalive `fetch`: `never ticked`
  - `session_slept` not surfaced: test 1 fails
  - interval kept after a 410: the new "not pinged again" assertion fails
- `pnpm test` in `runner/`: 2815/2815 pass.

### Checklist
- [ ] New/renamed example: added to `runner/config/frameworks.json` (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)); otherwise it won't appear on demos.handsontable.com
- [ ] New example: added a row to the tables in [README.md](README.md)
- [ ] Ran `pnpm build` (and `pnpm dev`) in the affected example/server-example locally

### Related issue(s):
1. [DEV-4231](https://app.clickup.com/t/123kvxejyv8)

fix(query-builder): keep value suggestions open when the editor re-renders

#### Description

- The query search value dropdown now stays open when the editor re-renders. Before, every render handed CodeMirror new extensions. When the cursor sat on an empty value like `service.name = '`, that closed the dropdown, for example when key suggestions loaded late.
- The CodeMirror extensions, `onChange` handler and `basicSetup` are now built once. They read the latest suggestions and run handler through refs, as `ListFilter/SearchBar` does.
- This fixes the flaky `fetches value suggestions when editing value context` test. The "keeps the value suggestions open when the key suggestions load" test now waits past CodeMirror's re-query, so it fails without this fix. Its old assertion ran before the dropdown closed.
- Stories already cover this: the Traces and Metrics explorer plays type `service.name = ` and wait for a value suggestion.

#### Issues closed by this PR

Closes https://github.com/SigNoz/pulse-pod/issues/782

fix(publicar-resposta-de-revisao): check the screen before replying about a visual change

## Why?

A reply to a review comment about a visual change was published saying that the screen had not been checked, and the person had to ask for the check. The reply should come after the check.

## What was done?

- `publicar-resposta-de-revisao` (0.4.3 → 0.5.0): Step 1 now says that, when the change alters what people see, the screen is checked before the reply, as `registrar-evidencia-visual` says, and the reply tells what was seen. It never says the screen was not checked.
- `registrar-evidencia-visual` entered `metadata.related`, because the body cites it.

## Comments

The skill check passes with the body under the token limit.

## How to test?

1. Ask for a reply to a review comment about a color or a layout.
2. The screen must be checked first, and the reply must say what was seen.

benchmarks.task_description:
Leave an uppercase uncountable last word alone

## What is wrong

An uncountable word is left alone when it is the whole string, or the last word in lowercase or CamelCase. But when the last word is in ALL CAPS after a space, `-`, `_` or `/`, it gets inflected:

```js
pluralize('SHEEP');            // 'SHEEP'        (ok)
pluralize('my sheep');         // 'my sheep'     (ok)
pluralize('mySheep');          // 'mySheep'      (ok)

pluralize('my SHEEP');         // 'my SHEEPs'    (expected 'my SHEEP')
pluralize('USER_INFORMATION'); // 'USER_INFORMATIONs'
singularize('new SERIES');     // 'new Series'   (expected 'new SERIES')
singularize('blue_JEANS');     // 'blue_JEAN'
```

The cause: `LAST_WORD_DASHED_REGEX` only finds a lowercase last word, and `LAST_WORD_CAMELIZED_REGEX` only finds one capital letter plus lowercase. An all-caps last word is found by neither, so the uncountable check never sees it.

## The fix

Let `LAST_WORD_DASHED_REGEX` also match an all-uppercase last word. The last word is only used for the uncountable check, and that check already lowercases the word. Nothing else changes.

## The test

Added `an uppercase uncountable last word is left alone` in `tests/unit/inflector-test.ts`. It covers space, `-`, `/` and `_`, for both `pluralize` and `singularize`, and checks that a normal all-caps word (`my CAR`) still gets inflected.

- Before the fix: 57 pass, 1 fail (the new test).
- After the fix: 58 pass.

I also ran the default rules over about 790k words (the system word list plus capitalized, uppercase and multi-word forms). The only outputs that changed were the 420 strings that end in an all-caps uncountable word.

test(api): the browser suite is not held to the API's read quota

## What changed

The browser fixture gives the API a throttle that lets the `api` attempt through, the read quota of 300 requests a minute per account and 600 per network. Every other limit applies as in production: login, registration, mail, MFA and token proofs.

- `BrowserSuiteThrottle` (in `src/testing/`) extends `PrismaIdentityThrottle`. It answers `api` with an allowed decision and passes every other attempt to the real store.
- `integrationApp` accepts a provider override by class (`{ token, useClass }`), next to the existing override by value, so Nest builds the throttle with its dependencies.
- `browserApp` puts that override first, and a test's own overrides still come after it.

## Why

`tenant.browser.spec.ts › creates scoped tokens the API accepts, and revokes a project token` failed intermittently:

- in CI on main at `b425efe`;
- twice in a row on #512, which does not touch that page;
- locally, once in three runs and once in four.

Each failure was a different 15-second wait: the *Create API token* button, `#token-project` and `#token-organization`.

I logged every API request and every 429 of the file:

- **What is refused.** The failing run got a 429 on `GET /api/v1/organizations`. The token form's organization list stayed empty, and Playwright waited for an option that never came. Passing runs got their 429s on requests the page retries.
- **Why.** Each step of the test reloads the whole application with `goto`, and each load reads about ten resources. The owner's page made 409 requests in its busiest minute, against a quota of 300 per account. All pages together made 576 from `127.0.0.1`, plus the test's own `context.request` calls, against 600 per network.

The browser suite checks screens, not the quota, and a person cannot click at that rate. The quota keeps its own integration tests (`identity-throttle.integration.spec.ts`, `api-token-authentication.integration.spec.ts`). The only 429 a browser test checks, in `security.browser.spec.ts`, is simulated by intercepting the response in the browser, and is unaffected.

## How it was tested

- `tenant.browser.spec.ts`, four runs in a row: 13/13 each time. Before the change, the same command failed one run in three, then one in four.
- The whole browser suite: 28/28.
- `api:typecheck` and `api:lint` pass.

## Security considerations

Test code only: the production throttle and its policy are unchanged. Credential limits still apply in the browser suite.

:bug:(financial-scraper): mettre un 403 Binance en quarantaine comme un 418 ou 451

## Ce qui change
`banOf` traite aussi un 403 comme un blocage : même quarantaine que 451 (Retry-After ou backoff doublé, alerte de fraîcheur, Lease en K8s), au lieu de rappeler Binance à chaque cycle.

## Pourquoi
Un 403 (WAF) n'était ni réessayé ni mis en quarantaine ; chaque appel pouvait aggraver le blocage. L'API publique Binance (sans clé, ADR-0026) n'a pas d'erreur d'authentification : 403 = WAF.

## Vérification
- `bun run test` financial-scraper : 449 passés (cas 403 ajouté à la table `it.each` existante)
- `biome check services/financial-scraper` : OK
- Non lancés : build:ts complet, gates (aucun fichier hors du service touché)

Simplifié : rien à simplifier.
